claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a naturally formed passive oxide film.
Under chloride-rich conditions, elevated temperature disrupts the integrity of Q235 steel's native oxide film relative to room-temperature exposure.
Elevated-temperature chloride exposure accelerates corrosion of Q235 steel relative to room-temperature exposure.
At room temperature, the native oxide film remains relatively intact.
An intact native oxide film suppresses corrosion by limiting ingress of aggressive species.
Elevated temperature kinetically accelerates oxidation of Q235 steel under the specified exposure conditions.
Accelerated oxidation at elevated temperature causes micro-cracking of the oxide film.
Accelerated oxidation at elevated temperature increases porosity of the oxide film.
Micro-cracking and increased porosity permit enhanced chloride penetration through the oxide film.
Enhanced chloride penetration accelerates localized corrosion.
Elevated-temperature samples will have greater weight loss than room-temperature samples.
Elevated-temperature samples will exhibit greater pitting intensity than room-temperature samples.
Elevated-temperature samples will exhibit measurable oxide-film morphological changes relative to room-temperature samples.
The temperature effect may vary with steel microstructure, alloy composition, environmental aggressiveness, experimental setup, and batch properties.
